lines: CASTLE LENDING LIBRARY. CLOSED BY ORDER OF THE COUNCIL.
The key is kept with the key to the forest gate, on the council's green tag. Enquiries to the Museum.
CASTLE LENDING LIBRARY. Tuesday to Saturday, nine until six. The STACKS off the LENDING DESK; the READING ROOM and REFERENCE off the STACKS, and REFERENCE opens onto the LENDING DESK as well.
Books are not to leave the building. Neither is anyone, after six.
Underneath, in pencil: the roof came in on the fourteenth. Nobody has been up to look.
Every page has been cut out close to the spine, neatly, by somebody with time. One is left.
It is about seeds, written for somebody who has never grown one. The last line is in the hand from your letter: it will not come up in the dark. Do it by day.
The page says the same thing. The cut edges are all one length.
Somebody has had a fire going on the reading room floor, and swept the ash into the grate afterwards.
They burned the chairs and not one book. You can sleep here.
LENDING DESK. Tickets to be shown going out.
STACKS. The library steps are to be put back on their mark after use.
REFERENCE. Books are not to be taken out.
Under it, in pencil: one left. The roof came in over it on the fourteenth.
